second rib: 2nd rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly. Serratus anterior attaches to the tuberosity on its upper surface.
sella turcica: Saddle-shaped structure on the upper surface of the body; contains the hypophysial fossa.
semimembranosus bursa: Between the semimembranosus tendon and the tibia; the commonest source of a Baker's (popliteal) cyst.
semimembranosus muscle: Deep hamstring inserting into the back of the medial condyle of the tibia; its tendon forms the oblique popliteal ligament.
semispinalis colli muscle: Cervical part of the superficial layer of the transversospinal group.
semispinalis thoracis muscle: Thoracic part of the superficial layer of the transversospinal group.
semitendinosus muscle: Hamstring inserting into the pes anserinus by its long tendon; used as a graft in ACL reconstruction. Tibial nerve.
septum of frontal sinuses: Thin bony septum separating the two frontal sinuses; it usually deviates from the midline.
septum of sphenoidal sinuses: Septum separating the two sphenoidal sinuses; a guide in transsphenoidal surgery.
serratus anterior muscle: Runs from the upper 8–9 ribs to the medial border of the scapula; protracts the scapula, holds it against the chest wall and allows the arm to rise above 90°. Long thoracic nerve damage causes a 'winged scapula'.
serratus posterior inferior muscle: Thin muscle from the T11–L2 spines to the lower four ribs.
serratus posterior superior muscle: Thin muscle from the upper thoracic spines to the 2nd–5th ribs; an accessory muscle of inspiration.
sesamoid bones of foot: Two small bones within the flexor hallucis brevis tendons beneath the 1st metatarsal head; they share in load transfer and can suffer sesamoiditis and fractures.
seventh rib: 7th rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.
short head of biceps brachii: Head arising from the coracoid process; both heads insert into the radial tuberosity, flexing and supinating the forearm. Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6).
short head of biceps femoris: Head arising from the linea aspera that flexes only the knee; supplied by the common fibular nerve. Both heads insert into the fibular head.
sinus of frontal bone: Paired air space within the frontal bone; it opens into the middle meatus through the frontonasal duct.
sinus of sphenoid bone: Air space in the body of the sphenoid; it opens into the sphenoethmoidal recess and is used as the transsphenoidal route in pituitary surgery.
sixth rib: 6th rib: a true (vertebrosternal) rib; its cartilage joins the sternum directly.
soleal line: Oblique line on the posterior surface; soleus arises from it.
soleus muscle: Flat muscle beneath gastrocnemius; it maintains posture when standing and, as a 'peripheral heart', aids venous return. Tibial nerve.
sphenoid bone: Butterfly-shaped bone in the middle of the skull base; the pituitary lies in its sella turcica. Nerves and vessels pass through the openings in its greater and lesser wings (optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramina rotundum, ovale and spinosum).
sphenoidal angle of parietal bone: Anteroinferior angle contributing to the pterion; the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery runs on its inner surface.
sphenoidal crest: Midline ridge on the front of the body; it contributes to the nasal septum.
sphenoidal lingula: Tongue-shaped projection on the lateral edge of the carotid sulcus.
sphenoidal margin of frontal bone: Margin that articulates with the sphenoid.
sphenoidal yoke: Flat bony area joining the two lesser wings (jugum).
sphenomandibular ligament: Ligament from the spine of the sphenoid to the lingula of the mandible; a remnant of Meckel's cartilage.
spinalis capitis muscle: Head part of the spinalis column, fused with semispinalis capitis.
spinalis colli muscle: Cervical part of the spinalis column; often poorly developed.
spinalis thoracis muscle: The most medial column of erector spinae; runs between the spinous processes.
spine of scapula: Bony ridge dividing the posterior surface in two; trapezius and deltoid attach to it.
spine of sphenoid bone: Spine at the posterior end of the greater wing; the sphenomandibular ligament attaches to it.
spinoglenoid notch: Notch between the spine and the glenoid; the suprascapular nerve passes through it to the infraspinous fossa.
spinous process: Backward-projecting process of the arch; ligaments and back muscles attach to it.
splenius capitis muscle: Bandage-like muscle from the nuchal ligament and upper thoracic spines to the mastoid; extends the head and turns it to the same side.
splenius colli muscle: Part of splenius extending to the transverse processes of the upper cervical vertebrae.
squamosal border of parietal bone: Border that articulates with the squamous part of the temporal bone.
squamosal margin of greater wing: Margin that articulates with the squamous part of the temporal bone.
squamous part of frontal bone: Broad squamous part forming the forehead.
squamous part of occipital bone: Broad posterior squamous part of the occipital bone.
squamous part of temporal bone: Thin squamous part forming the temple; a fracture here can cause an extradural haematoma.
stapes: The smallest bone in the body; its footplate closes the oval window and transmits vibration to the inner ear. Stapedius attaches to it; in otosclerosis the footplate becomes fixed.
sternal angle: Angle where the manubrium meets the body; at the level of the 2nd rib, it is used for counting ribs.
sternal articular surface: Articular surface at the medial end; forms the sternoclavicular joint with the sternum and the articular disc.
sternal end: Thick medial end of the clavicle; forms the only joint attaching the upper limb to the trunk.
sternocleidomastoid muscle: Muscle from the sternum and clavicle to the mastoid process, dividing the neck into anterior and posterior triangles. Nerves: accessory nerve (XI) and C2–C3. Acting alone it tilts the head to the same side and turns the face to the opposite side; it is shortened in torticollis.
sternocostal head of pectoralis major mu: Broad fibres arising from the sternum and costal cartilages; adduct and medially rotate the arm. Pectoral nerves.
sternohyoid muscle: Superficial infrahyoid muscle from the manubrium to the hyoid; supplied by the ansa cervicalis, it depresses the hyoid after swallowing.
sternothyroid muscle: Deep infrahyoid muscle from the manubrium to the thyroid cartilage; pulls the larynx down.
straight part of cricothyroid muscle: Vertical fibres of cricothyroid; they tilt the thyroid cartilage forwards and raise the pitch of the voice.
stylohyoid ligament: Ligament from the styloid process to the lesser horn of the hyoid; its ossification causes Eagle syndrome.
stylohyoid muscle: Runs from the styloid process to the hyoid, embracing the digastric tendon; supplied by the facial nerve.
